_what: PRONUNCIATION BRIDGE — PACK DATA. A learner who cannot read Thai script cannot pronounce what we serve. This file gives each bank phrase a Latin reading, keyed by the EXACT phrase the engine will render (male and female forms both present, so the lookup survives the form substitution).
_tool: PyThaiNLP 5.4.0 — word_tokenize(engine='newmm') then transliterate.romanize(engine='royin', the Royal Thai General System). GENERATED, never hand-typed.
_why_tokenize: Romanizing the whole phrase without tokenizing mashes it: ผมมาเที่ยวครับ -> 'phommathiaokhrap'. Tokenized, the same phrase reads 'phom ma thiao khrap'.
_LIMIT_NO_TONES: NO TONE MARKS — measured, not assumed. RTGS drops tones, and thai2rom_onnx returns the same string as royin on this version. Thai tones are lexical (they change the word), so this bridge gets you UNDERSTOOD; it does not make you RIGHT. Tone-marked readings need a curated dataset, not this library.
